payload.title: Fence Checkout recovery and finalization against replacement owners
payload.summary: P1 maintained source-ownership correctness. After a real child Checkout owner exits, recovery R1 authenticates its admitted edit and pauses immediately before actual Git restore. Recovery R2 completes, releasing that claim; a new valid Checkout B enters and writes its own admitted bytes. R1 resumes, restores B source to old HEAD and removes B owner.json/directory without an error. Independent tiny Git fixture observes value=2 become value=0 and new owner absent. No canonical source, grants, models or remote publication were involved.
payload.benefit: Bind each recovery/finalizer to the exact lease it acquired and serialize or fence the entire effect/release window against other recovery and new owners. Rechecking once before an await is insufficient. Permanent independent two-recoverer plus replacement-writer tests must preserve B bytes and B claim, stale normal finish must refuse, and a valid stopped-owner recovery must still restore only known edits. Retain default-No stopped-process precondition, raw source fingerprints, canonical-root checks, untracked custody, immutable history and schema compatibility; do not clear unknown owner state automatically. Full focused/static/protected100% production branch gate on final repair tree.
payload.uncertainty: The directory claim serializes __aenter__ but recover/finish do not fence owner identity across Git awaits or at owner deletion. This is a demonstrated concurrency defect, not a claim of historical main corruption or authority from Checkout. Repair remains in the current Checkout/Intake boundary; no generic transaction manager, scheduler, EventBus or new Agent framework. Existing v1 records need explicit safe compatibility; PID alone is not a lease epoch.
